facts.claim: The study found no support for the filter-bubble hypothesis regarding the effect of personalization on the content and source diversity of Google News.
facts.quote: we found no support for the filter-bubble hypothesis.

facts.claim: All of the recommendation logics under study proved to lead to a rather diverse set of recommendations that are on par with human editors.
facts.quote: We find that all of the recommendation logics under study proved to lead to a rather diverse set of recommendations that are on par with human editors

facts.claim: Basing recommendations on user histories can substantially increase topic diversity within a recommendation set.
facts.quote: basing recommendations on user histories can substantially increase topic diversity within a recommendation set.

facts.claim: Algorithmic systems structurally amplify ideological homogeneity, reinforcing selective exposure and limiting viewpoint diversity.
facts.quote: algorithmic systems structurally amplify ideological homogeneity, reinforcing selective exposure and limiting viewpoint diversity

facts.claim: Google News over-represents certain news outlets and under-represents other, highly frequented, news outlets.
facts.quote: we did, however, find a general bias in that Google News over-represents certain news outlets and under-represents other, highly frequented, news outlets.

facts.claim: Internet customization effectively isolates individuals from diverse opinions or materials, resulting in their exposure to only a select set of content.
facts.quote: A filter bubble refers to the phenomenon where Internet customization effectively isolates individuals from diverse opinions or materials, resulting in their exposure to only a select set of content.

research.angle: While some research shows algorithms amplify ideological homogeneity, other studies find that personalization does not necessarily reduce news diversity and can even match human editors in variety.
research.verdict: The evidence is mixed, with some studies confirming the existence of filter bubbles and others finding that the effects on news diversity may be exaggerated or manageable.
research.caveat: The evidence base suffers from geographic bias toward Western contexts, limited longitudinal research, and methodological fragmentation.
